problems.title: Complementary divisors on two dice
problems.question: n has12 positive divisors. The smaller6 label one die, larger6 the other. Find the probability their product equals n.
problems.idea: Reduce the question using the rule below, then check the allowed values.
formulas: Each small divisor d pairs with exactly one large divisor n/d.
steps: With an even divisor count n is nonsquare, so every complementary pair has one small and one large member.
There are6 successful ordered outcomes out of36.

problems.title: A car type given a speeding event
problems.question: P(truck)=.1,P(car)=.9. Speeding probabilities are.05 for trucks and.2 for cars. Given speeding, find P(car).
problems.idea: Reduce the question using the rule below, then check the allowed values.
formulas: Bayes: P(car|speed)=P(car)P(speed|car)/P(speed).
steps: The numerator is.18, so the ratio is.18/.185.

problems.title: Rearrange eight letters with one repeated pair
problems.question: Eight letters have exactly one letter repeated twice; all others are distinct. How many different arrangements?
problems.idea: Reduce the question using the rule below, then check the allowed values.
formulas: Count8! orders, then divide by2! for the identical pair.
steps: Each distinct arrangement is counted twice if the repeated letters are temporarily labeled.

problems.title: Angle between two lines in a square pyramid
problems.question: A regular square pyramid has height2 and base side4. K is midpoint of MC. Find the cosine between AK and MD.
problems.idea: Reduce the question using the rule below, then check the allowed values.
steps: AK=(3,3,1),MD=(−2,2,−2). Dot product=−2, lengths√19 and√12.
For the acute angle between unoriented lines take the absolute dot product.

problems.title: A scalar triple product
problems.question: a=(1,0,0),b=(0,2,0),c=(0,0,3). Find a·(b×c).
problems.idea: Reduce the question using the rule below, then check the allowed values.

problems.title: Sum solutions of a sign-dependent cosine equation
problems.question: Find the sum of roots of cosx=|x|/x in(−19.9,19.9).
problems.idea: Reduce the question using the rule below, then check the allowed values.
formulas: For x>0 need cosx=1; for x<0 need cosx=−1. Zero is excluded.
steps: Positive roots are2π,4π,6π; negative roots are−π,−3π,−5π.
Their sum is12π−9π.

problems.title: Two incorrect trigonometric identities
problems.question: Which printed identities are false?
problems.idea: Reduce the question using the rule below, then check the allowed values.
formulas: Correct formulas are cos²(α/2)=(1+cosα)/2 and sin(α−β)=sinαcosβ−cosαsinβ.
steps: The printed half-angle option uses cos2α instead of cosα. At α=π it gives0=1, false.
The printed sine-difference option gives cosαcosβ−sinαsinβ, which equals cos(α+β). At α=β=0 it gives0=1.
The other three listed double/triple-angle identities are correct.
problems.answer: Both options b and d are false.
problems.note: The question asks for one false identity, but the printed list contains two.

problems.title: Range of a sine plus its absolute value
problems.question: Find the range of2sin(3x+4)+2|sin(3x+4)|.
problems.idea: Reduce the question using the rule below, then check the allowed values.
formulas: For t∈[−1,1],2t+2|t| is0 if t≤0 and4t if t≥0.
steps: All values between0 and4 are attained.

problems.title: Lateral area of an oblique triangular prism
problems.question: A prism has equilateral base side6 and lateral edge5. An upper vertex projects to the lower base circumcenter. Find lateral area.
problems.idea: Reduce the question using the rule below, then check the allowed values.
formulas: The horizontal displacement is base circumradius2√3, giving height√(25−12)=√13.
steps: For the base edge opposite that vertex, the lateral-edge perpendicular component has length√(12+13)=5, giving face area6·5=30.
For each adjacent base edge the horizontal perpendicular component is√3; the full perpendicular component is√(3+13)=4, giving face area24.

problems.title: Difference of squared frustum base sides
problems.question: A regular square frustum has base sides a,b and lateral area12. Its apothem makes60° with the lower base. Find a²−b².
problems.idea: Reduce the question using the rule below, then check the allowed values.
formulas: Apothem l=(a−b)/(2cos60°)=a−b; lateral area=2(a+b)l.

problems.title: Principal inverse trigonometric compositions
problems.question: Which listed x satisfies arcsin(sinx)+arccos(cosx)=π?
problems.idea: Reduce the question using the rule below, then check the allowed values.
formulas: For x=2π/3, arcsin(sinx)=π/3 and arccos(cosx)=2π/3.
steps: Their sum isπ. For the other listed angles within[−π/2,π/2], the sum is x+|x|, which is notπ.

problems.title: A sine inequality true everywhere
problems.question: Which listed a makes sin²x−(a−2)sinx−2a≤0 for every real x?
problems.idea: Reduce the question using the rule below, then check the allowed values.
formulas: Set t=sinx∈[−1,1]; the polynomial factors(t+2)(t−a).
steps: Since t+2>0, the inequality for all t is equivalent to t≤a for every t≤1.
Thus a≥1. Among.5,−.5,−10,−2,199, only199 qualifies.
problems.answer: a=199 among the choices; the full set is a≥1.

problems.title: Length of a solution interval
problems.question: Find the interval length of solutions to √(x²)≥(√(x+8))².
problems.idea: Reduce the question using the rule below, then check the allowed values.
formulas: The domain is x≥−8 and the inequality is|x|≥x+8.
steps: For x≥0 it is impossible. For x<0 it becomes−x≥x+8, so x≤−4.
The solution is[−8,−4], of length4.

problems.title: Largest lateral face versus rectangular base
problems.question: A pyramid has rectangular base; two lateral faces are perpendicular to it, and the other two make60° and30° with it. Find largest-face area divided by base area.
problems.idea: Reduce the question using the rule below, then check the allowed values.
formulas: The apex projects to a rectangle vertex. With height h, adjacent base lengths are h/√3 and h√3.
steps: The inclined face with base h√3 has slant height h/sin60°=2h/√3, giving area h², equal to base area.
The other lateral-face ratios are1/√3,√3/2,1/(2√3), all smaller.

problems.title: An impossible cube section
problems.question: Which cannot be a plane section of a cube: triangle,quadrilateral,pentagon,hexagon,heptagon?
problems.idea: Reduce the question using the rule below, then check the allowed values.
formulas: A plane intersects each cube face in at most one section edge.
steps: A cube has only6 faces, so a nondegenerate section has at most6 sides.
Sections with3,4,5,6 sides are possible by cutting near a vertex or across successively more faces.

problems.title: Another root of a sine equation
problems.question: If sina=17/19, which listed angle also has sine17/19?
problems.idea: Reduce the question using the rule below, then check the allowed values.
formulas: sin(π−a)=sina and sine has period2π.
steps: sin(3π−a)=sin(π−a)=sina.

problems.title: Intersect two trigonometric inequalities
problems.question: Solve sinx>1/2 and cosx>1/2.
problems.idea: Reduce the question using the rule below, then check the allowed values.
formulas: In one period, sine requires π/6<x<5π/6 and cosine requires−π/3<x<π/3.
steps: Their intersection isπ/6<x<π/3.
Repeat with period2π.

problems.title: Count ordered pairs including boundary points
problems.question: How many(x,y)∈[0,2π]² solve sin(x+y)=0 and cos(x−y)=1?
problems.idea: Reduce the question using the rule below, then check the allowed values.
formulas: x−y=2πk, with k=−1,0,1.
steps: For k=0, x=y and sin2x=0, giving5 pairs at x=0,π/2,π,3π/2,2π.
The other k values give(0,2π),(2π,0), both valid.

problems.title: Inclination of the shorter oblique segment
problems.question: Two oblique lengths are13:12 and their planar projection lengths5:4. Find cosine of the shorter line’s inclination.
problems.idea: Reduce the question using the rule below, then check the allowed values.
formulas: Let lengths13t,12t and projections5u,4u. Their common squared height gives169t²−25u²=144t²−16u².
steps: Thus25t²=9u² and u=5t/3.
Cosine for the shorter segment is4u/(12t).

problems.title: Recover a dihedral angle
problems.question: A,B lie on a dihedral edge; AC,BD are perpendicular offsets on different faces. AC=AB=BD=CD/2. Find the angle.
problems.idea: Reduce the question using the rule below, then check the allowed values.
formulas: Let each of AC,AB,BD equal l. Then CD²=l²+l²+l²−2l²cosδ.
steps: Since CD=2l,4=3−2cosδ.
Thus cosδ=−1/2.

problems.title: Equal first and third binomial terms
problems.question: In(k+1)ⁿ, T₀=T₂ and k is natural. Which listed n is possible?
problems.idea: Reduce the question using the rule below, then check the allowed values.
formulas: T₀=kⁿ; T₂=C(n,2)kⁿ⁻², so k²=n(n−1)/2.
steps: For n=9 the right side is36=6².
For n=16,25,11,20,199 it is120,300,55,190,19701 respectively, none a square.

problems.title: A speaker followed immediately by one of two others
problems.question: Five speakers A,B,C,D,E are ordered, with A immediately followed by B or C. How many orders?
problems.idea: Reduce the question using the rule below, then check the allowed values.
formulas: Treat AB or AC as a two-person block.
steps: Each choice gives4!=24 orders of the block and three remaining speakers.
The two cases are disjoint, so add24+24.

problems.title: Identify the intersection of two strips
problems.question: Points satisfy x−y+2≤0,x−y+10≥0,2x−y−20≤0,2x−y−1≥0. What figure results?
problems.idea: Reduce the question using the rule below, then check the allowed values.
formulas: These are the strips−10≤x−y≤−2 and1≤2x−y≤20.
steps: Their boundary slopes are1 and2, giving a parallelogram with nonright angles.
In coordinates u=x−y,v=2x−y, adjacent edge vectors have lengths8√5 and19√2, unequal.
It is therefore neither a rhombus nor a rectangle.
problems.answer: A parallelogram that is neither a rhombus nor a rectangle.

problems.title: Area of an inclined square-prism section
problems.question: A plane inclined60° to a square prism’s bases passes through midpoints of two adjacent upper-base sides and two adjacent lower-base sides. Find section area divided by base area.
problems.idea: Reduce the question using the rule below, then check the allowed values.
formulas: Its projection is the square with two opposite corner triangles removed.
steps: Each removed triangle has legs a/2, area a²/8. Projection area=3a²/4.
Actual section area=projection/cos60°=3a²/2.

problems.title: Two reflected images of a triangle vertex
problems.question: In ABC,A=60°,C=45°. B₁ reflects B across AC; B₂ reflects B through midpoint of AC. Find angle B₁AB₂.
problems.idea: Reduce the question using the rule below, then check the allowed values.
formulas: Take AC horizontal. AB₁ makes angle−60° with AC, while AB₂ is parallel and equal to BC.
steps: Central reflection gives vector AB₂=BC. Because C=45°, this vector points45° below AC.
Thus the angle between the two rays is60°−45°.
